title: Too Long Among Those Who Hate Peace

verses.text: In my distress I cried to the LORD, and He answered me.
Deliver my soul, O LORD, from lying lips and a deceitful tongue.
What will He do to you, and what will be added to you, O deceitful tongue?
Sharp arrows will come from the warrior, with burning coals of the broom tree!
Woe to me that I dwell in Meshech, that I live among the tents of Kedar!
Too long have I dwelt among those who hate peace.
I am in favor of peace; but when I speak, they want war.

context.author: The title calls it “A song of ascents,” one of fifteen such psalms (120-134). They may have been sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem for the feasts; the Mishnah says the Levites sang them on the fifteen steps inside the Temple courts (Sukkah 5:4).
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship, and the nations called to join
context.mapLabel: MESHECH AND KEDAR, FAR FROM ZION
context.setting: The pilgrim songs begin far from Jerusalem. “In my distress I cried to the LORD, and He answered me. Deliver my soul, O LORD, from lying lips and a deceitful tongue” (vv.1-2). The liar will be repaid with “Sharp arrows… with burning coals of the broom tree!” (v.4). The singer feels like an exile: “Woe to me that I dwell in Meshech, that I live among the tents of Kedar! Too long have I dwelt among those who hate peace. I am in favor of peace; but when I speak, they want war” (vv.5-7).
context.custom: Meshech was a people in Anatolia, far to the north (Genesis 10:2; Ezekiel 38:2), and Kedar was a tribe of Arabian desert nomads, far to the southeast (Genesis 25:13; Isaiah 21:16-17). No one could live in both, so they are pictures of living among hostile, foreign people. The broom tree’s roots make charcoal that burns long and hot.
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 121: “I lift up my eyes to the hills.”
context.timelineBible: Jesus said, “Blessed are the peacemakers” (Matthew 5:9). Peter calls believers “foreigners and exiles” (1 Peter 2:11) in this world, and Hebrews says they were looking for a homeland (Hebrews 11:13-16). James describes the tongue as “a fire” (James 3:6).

overview.summary: The first pilgrim song is a cry from far away: surrounded by liars and people who love war, the singer longs for peace, and so for Zion.

customs.t: Black goat-hair tents of Kedar (Song of Songs 1:5).

archaeology.t: Assyrian annals mention the Arab tribe Qedar and its queens.
Assyrian texts name the Mushki of Anatolia, probably Meshech.

overview.discussion: “I am in favor of peace; but when I speak, they want war” (v.7). Where do I feel out of place, and how can I be a peacemaker there?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (all 150 in the app). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
